rv.q: This retelling of Noel Streatfeild’s 1936 novel about three adopted girls in interwar London is a total treat.
This is a splendid piece of inventive theatre that’s also great family entertainment.
Ballet Shoes is a perfect Christmas show, and if it didn’t warm the heart of even the biggest Grinch I would be thoroughly surprised.
Kendall Feaver ’s adaptation of the much-loved 1936 children’s novel by Noel Streatfeild is as nimble and twinkling as any dainty dancer’s fleet, satin-slippered feet.
It is a triumph for The National Theatre and an unmissable highlight of the season.
With limitless charm, wry humour and a sincere heart, this revival of Ballet Shoes is a must-see for all the family.
The end result is a thoroughly engaging and delightful tale of three sisters learning to rise above their own limitations and battle those restrictions imposed on them by society.
A full five star brava for this inspiring show!

cn.t: Critics praise this enchanting revival of Ballet Shoes for its imaginative staging and heartfelt charm, calling it splendid family entertainment with both whimsy and grit that makes for an ideal festive treat.
